title: Comparing and Ordering Numbers up to One Million
seo_title: Comparing and Ordering Numbers – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Order and compare whole numbers up to 1,000,000 using the signs <, > and =. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on comparing and ordering whole numbers up to one million with <, > and =, greatest and smallest numbers from digits and real-life problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Same length: compare from the left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A number with more digits is always greater: 100,000 > 99,999.
  • If two numbers have the same number of digits, compare from the left until the digits are different.
  • > means greater than, < means less than. The open side faces the bigger number.

Examples

Example

Compare 45,210 and 45,120

Same up to the hundreds: 2 > 1

Answer: 45,210 > 45,120

Example

Greatest number from 3, 8, 0, 5, 1

Biggest digits first

Answer: 85,310

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the first digits of numbers of different lengthsCount the digits first.
Turning the sign the wrong wayThe open side faces the bigger number.
Putting 0 first in the smallest numberA number cannot start with 0; put the smallest non-zero digit first.

faq.a: < means is less than and > means is greater than.
Compare them two at a time, or compare the highest place first.
Yes. It holds a place in a number.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the thousands place: 8 thousands is more than 4 thousands. So 98,341 > 94,381. 98,341 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the hundreds place: 5 hundreds is more than 3 hundreds. So 24,365 < 24,536, and 24,365 is the least.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the hundreds place: 6 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds. So 622,618 > 622,449.

items.q: Three towns have these populations: 14,982 people, 14,289 people and 12,489 people. Which list shows the numbers from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. 12,489 < 14,289, because in the thousands place 2 < 4. 14,289 < 14,982, because in the hundreds place 2 < 9. So the order is 12,489; 14,289; 14,982.
